sections.h2: Where do Mackinac County deeds get filed?
sections.html:
The county's Register of Deeds works from the first floor of the Mackinac County Courthouse at 100 S. Marley in St. Ignace, and the phone line is (906) 643-7306. The County Treasurer is one floor up (second floor, Room 30, phone (906) 643-7318), and the Equalization Department sits in the Courthouse Annex, Room 120, at (906) 643-7310. A seller who needs a deed filed, a tax certificate and a parcel record can finish all three errands in one courthouse complex.

The county is mostly water. Of its 2,101 square miles, 1,079 are lake, because Mackinac County has shoreline on both Lake Huron and Lake Michigan at the Straits of Mackinac. The 2020 census counted 10,834 people. St. Ignace is the seat and the northern end of the Mackinac Bridge, and Mackinac Island is the other city. Naubinway is a census-designated place, and the Sault Tribe holds two small territories, one near St. Ignace and one in Clark Township.

Getting around shapes how people sell here. I-75 and US 2 serve the mainland, ferries run from St. Ignace and Mackinaw City to Mackinac Island, and M-185 around the island bans all motor vehicles except emergency and service vehicles. The nearest scheduled airline service is at Chippewa County International in Sault Ste. Marie or Pellston Regional. Owners who live far from the courthouse should use the mail option below.

sections.h2: Can a Mackinac County deed be sent in by mail or e-recording?
sections.html:
Yes to both. Per the register's recording page, nobody has to appear in person, and documents with the right fee can go by mail, UPS or FedEx. Electronic filers can route through CSC E-Recording Solutions, Simplifile or EPN E Recording Partners Network, each with its own price list.

Staff offer a service most counties skip: they will look over a draft before you submit it. The office cannot write a private legal document or advise you, but it will check a draft against the recording rules. That can save a round trip across the Straits. Other handy points from the office's notes:

  • Include a self-addressed return envelope so the original comes back sooner.
  • In a deed the grantor is the seller and the grantee is the buyer.
  • Copy the legal description from the prior deed or a new survey, and avoid the shortened version printed on a tax statement unless someone has verified it.
  • Blanket assignments and blanket releases are accepted.
  • Forms are sold at office supply stores or available online, and a local title company may supply one.

sections.h2: What fees apply at the Mackinac County register?
sections.html:
One flat charge covers any document up to any length. Under MCL 600.2567 that is $30.00, in force since October 1, 2016. The office's fee page notes that $4 of it goes to the state survey and remonumentation fund. A deed with a warranty clause also needs a treasurer's certificate for $5.00, and the register suggests a single $35.00 check. If you mail the deed, its staff pick up the certificate for you.

Mackinac County Register of Deeds charges, from the office's fee pages

A certified copy must reproduce the whole document. The fee page also mentions a 2016 push by the state's registers of deeds to stop private companies from selling deeds to residents at inflated prices. The office's own rate is the page price above.

sections.h2: How much transfer tax will a Mackinac County seller owe?
sections.html:
Seller-side transfer tax runs $4.30 for every $500 of price, rounded up for any leftover amount. That is the county's 55 cents (MCL 207.504) plus the state's $3.75, which the register lists in its FAQ. The statute puts the burden on the grantor.

Try an $820,000 Straits-view property: 1,640 units of $500, so $902 to the county and $6,150 to the state, or $7,052 combined. A modest $140,000 mainland house comes to $1,204. The deed must state the full price on its face, or a valuation affidavit goes with it at no filing charge, and the deed must say the affidavit is attached. Tax stamps are bought where the land sits, and land in two counties needs a stated split.

Exemptions appear on the register's county and state exemption pages and in MCL 207.526. Gifts to children and grandchildren, foreclosure transfers and court-ordered transfers are among them. An exemption has to be written on the face of the deed, so settle it with your closing agent before signing.

sections.h2: What if the house is behind on a mortgage or taxes?
sections.html:
Mackinac County's register and treasurer jointly run a foreclosure prevention page, and it explains a ranking that surprises many owners: a tax foreclosure takes precedence over a mortgage foreclosure. Once a mortgage foreclosure starts, the office says the owner keeps control of the property for 6 months, or 12 months if the parcel is larger than 3 acres, and can refinance or sell during that time.

The page also offers a set of practical steps:

  • Call the lender early and read every letter it sends.
  • Look for a HUD-approved housing counselor, since counseling is free or low cost.
  • Contact the Michigan State Housing Development Authority about its Save the Dream program.
  • Do not pay a company that promises to stop a foreclosure, and never sign a paper that appoints someone to act for you.

On the tax side, the County Treasurer collects delinquent property taxes for the local units and handles the summer auction of foreclosed properties under Public Act 123. The Equalization Department hosts a property and delinquent tax search and a list of each local unit's assessor and treasurer. A sale that pays off the balance before the redemption window ends is one way out.

sections.h2: What does a recorded deed change for property tax in Mackinac County?
sections.html:
The register notifies the assessor of recorded transfers each month, and the new owner must also file with the local assessor within 45 days under MCL 211.27a. A transfer of ownership resets the following year's taxable value to the state equalized value. Moves to a spouse, and residential moves to a parent, child, sibling or grandchild with no commercial use, do not count.

The statute counts a rental of fewer than 15 days in a year as non-commercial, which matters for a cottage that sees a few weekend guests. Longer rentals fall outside that carve-out. Ask the assessor for the parcel's current taxable value before you list.

The register also processes passport applications Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m., which is useful to know if a seller who is relocating needs travel documents at the same visit.

faqs.q: Is it $30 or $35 to file a deed in Mackinac County?
faqs.a: It is $35.00 when the deed contains a warranty clause, made up of the $30.00 filing fee and the $5.00 treasurer's certificate, and $30.00 when it does not. Each extra instrument released in one document adds $3.00.

faqs.q: Who writes the deed for a Mackinac County sale?
faqs.a: A title company or attorney should draft it. Register staff cannot draft private legal documents, though they will review a draft for compliance with the recording rules before you submit it.

faqs.q: What is the combined transfer tax rate for a Mackinac County home?
faqs.a: The combined rate is $4.30 per $500 of price or fraction. A $300,000 sale gives 600 units, so $330 to the county and $2,250 to the state, for $2,580 in total.

faqs.q: Who runs the foreclosure auction in Mackinac County?
faqs.a: The County Treasurer, at 100 S. Marley, Room 30, handles the summer auction of foreclosed properties. Call (906) 643-7318, or use the property and delinquent tax search on the Equalization Department page.

faqs.q: How long can an owner stay after a Mackinac County mortgage foreclosure?
faqs.a: Six months, or twelve months if the parcel has more than 3 acres, according to the county's foreclosure prevention page. During that window the owner can refinance or sell.
